extracted.intended_audience: general readers and researchers interested in comedy, comedians, and close-up magic (Wikipedia audience)
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards relevant to producing, presenting, or evaluating controversial/shock-oriented stand-up comedy (with overlap into close-up magic performance and venue/regulatory responses). Covers artistic style, audience expectations, community norms, legal/regulatory limits, and measures of success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controversial / black comedy as a recognized style
rubrics_metrics.description: Described as "notorious for his controversial brand of black comedy."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page frames shock, taboo, and politically incorrect material as an intentional stylistic choice that defines the performer's public persona and critical reception. Examples: use of extreme insults, offensive references, and deliberately transgressive sketches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience suspension of beliefs / willingness to accept offence
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz has said that audiences going to see a comedian should "suspend their beliefs."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This frames an expectation that audiences attending such performances temporarily accept extreme premises and provocative material; performers and critics may use this to judge whether an audience was prepared or whether material violated implicit expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserving surprise as an essential element of comedy
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz published an open letter asking reviewers not to quote his material, stating that "a very important element of comedy is surprise, and it can often make the difference between a show that works and one that does."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance for presenters and reviewers: avoid reproducing punchlines or routines in reviews or online (to protect the efficacy of live performance). Also a production choice to control spoilers when releasing recordings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical excellence in close-up magic and sleight of hand
rubrics_metrics.description: He is "widely acclaimed as one of the best close-up magicians in the world" and "an accomplished practitioner of sleight of hand, having written several books on magic and invented several conjuring innovations."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For combined comedy/magic acts, craft and technical skill in magic are a distinct evaluative dimension separate from comedic transgression; publications, inventions, books, and peer recognition are cited as markers of excellence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regulatory limits on obscene/offensive language (cumulative effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Broadcasting Standards Commission concluded that the repeated use of the words "fuck" and "cunt" "had a cumulative effect that was both excessive and unnecessary."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory evaluation can consider cumulative exposure to obscene language across a programme/series, not just isolated instances. Broadcasters and producers must account for such standards and the potential for reprimand or sanctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Venue ethical/values standards (racism/sexism/homophobia/misogyny intolerance)
rubrics_metrics.description: A venue cancelled his show, later clarifying this was due to "racism, sexism, homophobia and misogyny" and that "the material presented at his first show is not acceptable and does not align with our values."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Venues and festivals may apply institutional value statements that can override artistic license; compliance with venue standards (or risks of cancellation) is an evaluative/practical criterion when booking or programming controversial performers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal risk when referencing allegations or named individuals
rubrics_metrics.description: An album was quickly withdrawn from sale due to fears of being sued for libel by Jimmy Savile after Sadowitz referenced rumours of the TV personality being a paedophile.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers and performers must weigh libel/defamation risk when including allegations about real people; such concerns can lead to withdrawals, edits, or self-censorship even if material seems topical or justified later.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of shock/stunts and boundaries of decency
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of shock tactics: appearing wearing a kilt and a huge plastic phallus spraying the audience; simulated sodomy and food-smearing in shows; exposure and indecency allegations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Shock stunts may deliver strong audience reactions but carry risks: legal/health/safety concerns, venue or regulator backlash, alienation of parts of an audience, and reputational consequences. Assess appropriateness and downstream effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical conduct, audience safety, and harassment risks
rubrics_metrics.description: Incidents include spitting in the face of a heckler, stripping naked and running across the stage, and exposing his penis to an audience member.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical actions toward audience members or indecent exposure raise safety, assault, and harassment issues; such conduct is an evaluative dimension for acceptability and legality beyond comedic intent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community norms and acceptance within adjacent professional communities
rubrics_metrics.description: Outbursts of savage comedy during conjuring shows have sometimes alienated him from the more conservative magic community.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different professional communities (e.g., magicians versus alternative comedy circuits) have their own norms; violating those can affect bookings, peer support, and credibility within those fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Influence and originality (impact vs imitation)
rubrics_metrics.description: He "has influenced a generation of comedians," but he states "politically incorrect comedy: it's me, and it's been ripped off by loads and loads of comics."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measures of a comedian's significance include influence on others and claims to originality; evaluators may distinguish pioneering from derivative acts when assessing artistic contribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commercial success and popularity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Cited indicators include being voted among Channel 4's 100 Greatest Stand-Ups, sold-out shows, breaking box office records, and tours selling out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Poll rankings, box-office/ticket-sales, sold-out runs, and extended tours serve as pragmatic measures of commercial success and audience demand, separate from critical or ethical judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of recorded/distributed material to manage reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Sadowitz removed clips from YouTube and torrent sites within hours; he shelved a DVD release to avoid audiences comparing him to other comics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions about releasing recordings (DVDs, clips) affect how work is perceived and can be used strategically to protect surprise, avoid mischaracterisation, or control comparisons; restrict distribution when artistic or reputational goals demand it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial / critical practice: avoid reproducing material in reviews
rubrics_metrics.description: He asked reviewers not to quote his material because surprise matters to the success of the show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers and journalists should consider the performer's request and the role of spoilers; ethical editorial practice may differ for television/online clips versus live performance, but reproducing key punchlines can materially affect a show's impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural confrontation as a deliberate creative aim
rubrics_metrics.description: The Guardian noted Sadowitz "shook up the right-on values of the 80s alternative comedy circuit with his willingness to say the unsayable."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some comedians intentionally confront or subvert prevailing cultural attitudes; critics evaluating such work should assess intent, effect, and whether the confrontation achieves artistic/critical goals or merely provokes.
